Notes from a Summer Job

I spent last summer washing dishes at a diner in Dayton. The work was hot and loud, and I loved it.

References to the owner's temper were a running joke among the cooks; nobody took them seriously. She yelled, then she fed us.

Notes

That was the word she wrote on the whiteboard every morning: a list of what had gone wrong the day before. Some days the list was long.

Appendix A of my life, if there were one, would be that diner.

Bibliography is not something I expected to love, but in Professor Hall's class I did. Sources consulted early make the later work easier.
